AthlasX_Player_Onboarding: The player onboarding flow is a single-page, 9-step wizard rendered by app/onboarding/player/PlayerProfileWizard.tsx, reached at /onboarding/player once a player account signs up (role player). Each step auto-saves to its own backend table as soon as the player clicks “Save & Continue,” so progress always survives a refresh or a dropped session. Step labels are: Basic Info, Aadhaar Verification, Physical, Cricket, Bio, Media, Performance, Fitness (optional), Consent.

This supersedes an older 12-step flow (onboarding_progress / 12-step tables further below still exist in the schema for historical/score-weighting reasons, but the wizard a player actually completes today is the 9-step PlayerProfileWizard).

Fields: first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, city, state, country. Age is computed client-side from date_of_birth; under-18 triggers a visible “minor — parental consent required” hint that carries through to Step 9. Saved via POST /api/player/profile/save into player_profiles.
The player enters a 12-digit Aadhaar number (auto-masked as they type) and requests an OTP — POST /api/onboarding/aadhaar/initiate.
OTP confirmation — POST /api/onboarding/aadhaar/confirm — also sends the Step-1 date_of_birth as declared_dob so the server can flag a >6-month discrepancy between declared and Aadhaar-verified DOB.

The server returns a masked Aadhaar string, the verified DOB, computed age, an is_minor flag, and verification points. The raw Aadhaar number is never stored — only masked_aadhaar and verified_dob persist, in aadhaar_verification.
“Save & Continue” on this step is disabled until verification succeeds.
Fields: height_cm, weight_kg, dominant_hand. Saved into player_profiles.
Fields: playing_role (Batsman / Bowler / All-Rounder / WK), secondary_role, batting_style, bowling_style, wicket_keeper flag, school_team, club_team, district_team, state_team, academy_id.
Selecting WK as primary role auto-sets wicket_keeper and clears bowling_style (keepers don’t bowl); the bowling_style field disables accordingly.
academy_id is set via a debounced live search against GET /api/academies/search?q=…, letting a player optionally link to an existing academy record.
Free-text fields: bio, aspirations, strengths, improvement_areas. Saved into player_profiles.
Beta, link-only: the player pastes a YouTube (or R2/S3/Cloudinary) video URL plus an optional title. There is no direct file upload yet.
Each add calls POST /api/player/media, removal calls DELETE /api/player/media; rows live in player_media.
At least one video is required — the wizard blocks advancing past this step with zero media rows.
Fields: matches_played, runs_scored, wickets_taken, highest_score, best_bowling. Saved into player_profiles.
Fields: yoyo_score, sprint_30m, run_2km. Marked optional in the stepper; skipping is allowed via a dedicated “Skip” button. These boost AthlasX Score but are not required to submit.

If the player is a minor (computed from Step 1’s DOB), parent_name and parent_phone (plus optional parent_email) become required, alongside all four consent checkboxes: profile_visibility_ok, media_upload_ok, scout_contact_ok, data_usage_ok.
Consent is saved via POST /api/player/consent into player_consents — a new row per consent event (signed_at timestamped), not an update-in-place.
The server re-validates everything independently of the client — missing items are returned as a structured array so the wizard can tell the player exactly what to fix:
Basic Profile — first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, state all required.
Cricket Profile — playing_role and batting_style required; bowling_style required unless the player is a keeper (playing_role = WK or wicket_keeper = true).
Performance Stats — matches_played must be present (including 0).
Videos — at least one player_media row must exist.
Minor consent gate — if isMinor(date_of_birth), the latest player_consents row must have parent_name, parent_phone, and all four boolean consents true, or submission is rejected with minor: true.
player_profiles.profile_status → 'Pending Approval', visibility stays 'Private', submitted_at = NOW().

users.account_status flips 'pending' → 'active' (only if it was still 'pending') — this is what stops the dashboard from looping the player back into onboarding. The profile itself stays gated behind AthlasX admin approval before going Live/visible to scouts.
Player lands on /dashboard/player after a successful submit.

AthlasX_Coach_Onboarding: Coach onboarding has two distinct paths. This document covers the self-signup wizard (app/onboarding/coach/CoachOnboardingWizard.tsx, route /onboarding/coach) for an account that signed up directly with role coach. A second path exists for coaches added by an academy via an invite link (/coach/register?token=…) — those coaches never see this wizard; they redeem the invite directly. Both paths write into the same coach_registry table.
Email is read-only from sign-up. coach_name defaults to the sign-up name but is editable — this is the display name academies and players will see.
academy_club (free text, e.g. “MRF Pace Foundation”). Left blank, a coach can still complete onboarding as fully independent — but evaluation permissions stay off until an academy admin links them.
official_id (required — BCCI L1/L2, NIS, NCA, or federation ID).
cert_url (required — link to a scan of the certificate, ID card, or federation page).

AthlasX reviews these credentials before granting can_submit_evaluations and can_submit_fitness_assessments. A verified coach’s rating is what moves a linked player into the Performance Verified trust tier.
Read-only summary (sign-up name, email, display name, academy/club, official ID, certification link, current coach status). Submitting calls a save followed by POST /api/coach/profile/submit.
Caller must be authenticated with role coach. The route reads coach_registry and checks:
Academy / Club — required at submit time, even though Step 2’s UI describes it as optional for a fully independent coach — in practice the submit gate currently requires it to be filled.

coach_registry.coach_status → 'PENDING_REVIEW', but only if the row’s current status is still DRAFT or PENDING_REVIEW (the WHERE clause excludes APPROVED/REJECTED rows from being reset). No users.account_status change happens in this route.
users  (one row per account, all four roles share this table)

Allowed role values (soft-enforced in app code, not a DB CHECK constraint): player, parent, academy_admin, coach, scout, tournament_organizer, athlasx_admin. Live data also contains the legacy admin variants admin and sportx_admin from earlier naming.
coach_registry  (14 columns, live schema — one row per coach, either self-signup or invite-redeemed)
FK → coach_invites(id) ON DELETE SET NULL — set only on the invite-redemption path
no FK ON DELETE clause — admin who reviewed
two columns exist; rejection_reason is the spec-aligned one added later
0 — count of players awaiting this coach’s evaluation
coach_invites  (invite-redemption path — issued by a player or an academy)
FK → users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE — the player/academy who issued the invite
unique, used in the redemption link
coach_registry.coach_status: DRAFT → PENDING_REVIEW (self-submit) → APPROVED / REJECTED (AthlasX admin, or the linked academy).
Approval unlocks can_submit_evaluations and can_submit_fitness_assessments — these are permission flags read at the point of use, not columns visible in coach_registry itself.

AthlasX_Academy_Onboarding: Academy onboarding is a single-page form (app/onboarding/academy/AcademyProfileForm.tsx, route /onboarding/academy) for an account with role academy_admin. Unlike the player and coach/scout flows, there is no step-by-step wizard — every section (Identity, Location, Contact, Social Links, Programs) is on one scrollable page with a manual “Save draft” button plus a single “Submit for Approval” action.
Fields: city (required), state (required, dropdown of Indian states), country (defaults to ‘India’).
Fields stored together as a single JSON object social_links: instagram, twitter, youtube, linkedin.
age_groups — multi-select chips: U-10, U-12, U-14, U-16, U-19, U-23, Senior.
facilities — multi-select chips: Indoor nets, Outdoor nets, Turf wicket, Floodlights, Gym, Pool, Hostel, Video analysis, Bowling machine.
specialties — multi-select chips: Pace bowling, Spin bowling, Batting, Wicket-keeping, All-rounder development, Junior cricket, Women’s cricket.
All three Programs fields are stored as Postgres TEXT[] arrays, toggled on/off per chip click — there is no limit on how many can be selected.
“Save draft” — POST /api/academy/profile/save — can be called any number of times with a partial form; no validation beyond what the column types enforce.
“Submit for Approval” — calls save first, then POST /api/academy/profile/submit. On success the admin redirects to /dashboard/academy.
Caller must be authenticated with role academy_admin. Missing fields are returned as a structured list:
Location — both city and state required.

academies.profile_status → 'Pending Approval', verification_status → 'PENDING', submitted_at = NOW(). There is no automatic users.account_status activation in this route (unlike the player flow) — academy accounts remain gated on verification_status until an admin acts.

AthlasX_Scout_Onboarding: Scout onboarding is a 4-step wizard (app/onboarding/scout/ScoutOnboardingWizard.tsx, route /onboarding/scout) for an account with role scout. Steps: Scout Profile, Organization & Affiliation, Scouting Preferences, Review & Submit. This implements Part 1 of the AthlasX_Onboarding_Workflows_Scout_Coach spec.

The live scout_profiles table (columns documented below) is NOT the table defined in prisma/0001_initial.sql — that file describes an earlier, aspirational schema (scout_name, scout_type enum, pref_min_age/max_age, etc.) that was never applied. The columns below were confirmed directly against the live database, not against either schema file, per the project’s known schema-drift gotcha.
Name and email are read-only, pulled from sign-up. The only editable field is designation (free text, e.g. “Talent Scout”, “Head Scout”, “Selector”) — required to advance.
org_type (required, one of: Independent, Franchise, State, Country, Academy).
proof_url (required — link to an ID card, official letter, or LinkedIn profile).

Hard rule shown on this step: scouts can never contact minors directly, even after Minor-Cleared (L2) — all contact with a minor player is routed via the player’s parent or guardian. This is a policy statement in the UI, not (yet) a server-enforced constraint visible in this flow.
preferred_age_groups — multi-select chips: U16, U19, U23, Open.
preferred_roles — multi-select chips: Batter, Bowler, All-Rounder, WK.
preferred_regions — multi-select chips, one per Indian state (18 states listed).
These do not restrict search — they only tune AthlasX’s discovery-feed suggestions and can be changed later.
Read-only summary of every field collected, plus the current verification level. Submitting calls a save (to flush any pending step) followed by POST /api/scout/profile/submit.
Caller must be authenticated with role scout. The route reads the scout_profiles row and checks:
Years of Experience — required (years_experience must not be null; 0 is valid).
Scouting Preferences — at least one of preferred_age_groups or preferred_roles must be non-empty.

scout_profiles.profile_status → 'Pending Approval', submitted_at = NOW(). The row’s verification_level stays at 'L0' until an AthlasX admin promotes it — unlike the player flow, there is no automatic users.account_status activation here; L0/L1 IS the gate. Per the route’s own comment, adult-profile search is already available at L0; L1 (Verified) and L2 (Minor-Cleared) are separate admin-granted promotions.
